<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is an open-source, full-featured Zsh prompt theme (Spaceship Prompt).  
   - It’s a shell plugin/library that augments the Zsh prompt with contextual information (Git status, runtime versions, battery, etc.).  
   - It also includes a documentation site (MkDocs), test suite, and CI/CD pipelines for releases (npm, Homebrew, Docker).

2. High-Level Components  
   A. User Environment  
      • Zsh shell (v5.2+) with Powerline/Nerd font  
      • User’s dotfiles (e.g., ~/.zshrc) that source the plugin  
   B. Core Library  
      • spaceship.zsh + spaceship.zsh-theme  
      • lib/ — core modules: cache, CLI, config, prompts, sections loader, utils  
      • sections/ — individual prompt segments (git, docker, node, python, etc.)  
   C. Configuration  
      • zstyle and environment variables for per-directory and global settings  
   D. External Dependencies  
      • Shell built-ins and Zsh APIs  
      • External CLIs (git, hg, docker, kubectl, npm, cargo, python, etc.)  
   E. Tests  
      • tests/ — unit tests (shunit2) and stubs for various CLIs  
      • scripts/tests — test runner  
   F. Documentation  
      • docs/ and mkdocs.yml — MkDocs site structure, assets, multilingual content  
      • scripts/docs (via GitHub Actions) → Netlify (deployment)  
   G. CI/CD & Distribution  
      • .github/workflows/ — validate.yaml (lint/tests), docs.yml (build/deploy docs), docker.yml, homebrew.yml, release.yml, deps.yaml  
      • npm registry, Homebrew (Brew formula), AUR, GitHub Releases, Docker Hub  

3. Interactions & Data Flow  
   1. User starts a new Zsh session → ~/.zshrc sources spaceship.zsh  
   2. spaceship.zsh-theme loads:  
      - Sources lib/*.zsh modules  
      - For each enabled section, calls its hook in sections/*.zsh  
      - Each section invokes external CLI or reads environment (e.g., “git status”, “node --version”)  
      - Aggregates outputs, formats using prompts module  
      - Renders final prompt string back into Zsh PS1  
   3. User enters commands, repeats above per prompt redraw  
   4. Developers run tests: scripts/tests invokes tests/*.test.zsh with stubs for each section  
   5. CI pipeline triggers on PR/merge:  
      - Run lint & tests (validate.yaml)  
      - Build & publish docs via MkDocs to Netlify (docs.yml)  
      - Build Docker image & push (docker.yml)  
      - Publish npm package and GitHub Release (release.yml)  
      - Update Homebrew formula (homebrew.yml)  

4. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles  
   - Modular design: each “section” is self-contained, discoverable, and configurable  
   - Plugin architecture: lib/core dispatches to hooks in sections folder  
   - Convention over configuration: defaults via zstyle, override per‐directory  
   - Test stubs isolate external dependencies for reliable unit tests  
   - Documentation as code: MkDocs config + markdown under docs/  

5. Tailoring the Diagram for This Open-Source CLI Tool  
   - Emphasize the plugin core + section modules as central blocks  
   - Show how configuration (zstyle/env) flows into core modules  
   - Illustrate dependencies on external CLIs (git, docker, languages) as side-car services  
   - Depict CI/CD workflows as separate pipeline blocks feeding into distribution channels (npm, Homebrew, Docker Hub, Netlify)  

6. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Components & Labels:  
     • “User Shell” (Zsh)  
     • “Spaceship Core” (spaceship.zsh + lib/)  
     • “Sections” (sections/*.zsh)  
     • “Config” (zstyle, env vars)  
     • “External CLIs” (Git, Docker, Node, etc.)  
     • “Test Suite” (tests/, stubs)  
     • “Docs” (MkDocs)  
     • “CI/CD Pipelines” (.github/workflows)  
     • “Distribution” (npm, Homebrew, Docker Hub, Netlify)  
   - Arrows:  
     • Shell → Core (load)  
     • Core → Sections (dispatch calls)  
     • Sections → External CLIs (invoke)  
     • Core → Shell PS1 (render)  
     • Dev Workflow → CI/CD → Distribution  
     • Docs Source → MkDocs → Netlify  
   - Styles:  
     • Use distinct colors for runtime blocks (green), dev/pipeline blocks (blue), external services (orange)  
     • Group related modules into swimlanes or clustered shapes (Core, Sections, Tests, CI/CD)  
     • Annotate configurations and hooks clearly  

7. Detail & Completeness  
   - Capture every architectural element: core modules, extension points (sections), configs, test runner, docs builder, CI workflows, distribution targets  
   - Don’t simply list files; group by responsibility and show interactions  
   - Ensure the diagram clearly conveys how the prompt is built at runtime and how the project is developed, tested, documented, and released  
</explanation>
